_what: Why 34 recall skips survive the D187 (1) cold-pricing fix at r1 s4 and s5. Read DIRECTLY from release_infeasible_events, which the P0 instrumentation shipped with the fix; the previous diagnosis had to reconstruct every one of these with a declared proxy.

H1_belief_COLD_while_engine_warm.verdict: REFUTED AT s4, SMALL BUT NON-ZERO AT s5. My first wording said 'refuted with a zero' and that was s4-only.
H1_belief_COLD_while_engine_warm.evidence: s4: all 34 skips record readiness GPU-WARM, not one COLD. s5: 12 of 15 GPU-WARM and 3 COLD. So a belief error contributes nothing at s4 and at most 3 of 15 at s5.
H1_belief_COLD_while_engine_warm.so: a belief fix cannot explain the residual at s4 and could address at most a fifth of a much smaller residual at s5. It is not the main lever at either seed.
H1_belief_COLD_while_engine_warm.register: counts per seed, not pooled; s6 and s7 had not landed when this was written

H2_telemetry_never_written_by_warm_or_to.evidence: s4: only 7 of 34 prefixes are exact multiples of 1024, the build-piece size; the rest are values like 2,169, 10,361, 12,592 and 20,608 that built_tokens cannot produce, so last_telemetry_cached_tokens IS written and IS used. s5 is less clear-cut on this test, 12 of 15 being multiples, but s5's residual is only 15 skips and two of its three non-multiples are large (18,352 and 21,872), which again only telemetry can produce. Consistent with the code: the corrector's guard at coordinator.py:1702 is `if sub.session_id:`, SESSION-based not KIND-based, so warms and touches reach it and only monitors (no session) are excluded.
H2_telemetry_never_written_by_warm_or_to.so: the user's hypothesis that warms and touches leave pricing blind is not what is happening

H3_the_queue_term_not_the_size_term.verdict: SUPPORTED, and this is the finding
H3_the_queue_term_not_the_size_term.evidence: s4: the size term ALONE exceeds the slack in only 9 of 34 skips; the other 25 are feasible on their own size and are refused only once queued_uncached_ahead is added (p50 1,496, max 9,839). s5: 7 of 15 by size alone, 8 needing the queue, with a HIGHER queue (p50 3,684, max 10,720). So the queue is the majority channel at s4 and about half at s5.
H3_the_queue_term_not_the_size_term.so: after the pricing fix the residual skips are a QUEUE question, not a size question

THE_QUEUE_INPUT_IS_THE_WRONG_QUANTITY_AN.what: the re-check passes queued_uncached_ahead=self._uncached_in_flight, which decrements at COMPLETION and therefore includes the DECODE TAIL of requests whose prefill is already finished. The work actually ahead of a request in the prefill queue is the submit-to-FIRST-TOKEN quantity, which already exists in the coordinator as the D179 W tracker (self._w.total()).
THE_QUEUE_INPUT_IS_THE_WRONG_QUANTITY_AN.already_on_the_record: share_admission.py's own module docstring states this distinction and says _uncached_in_flight is 'the right queue input for the D174 budget charge and the wrong resource here'. It was applied to W and NOT to the re-check's queue term.
THE_QUEUE_INPUT_IS_THE_WRONG_QUANTITY_AN.WHY_I_DID_NOT_CHANGE_IT_TONIGHT: I cannot establish from the committed artefacts WHICH in-flight definition the D162 fit used as its regressor. cost_model_gate_d162.json records the coefficient and that the term varies (min 0, p50 746, max 9,933) but not whether the regressor was completion-based or first-token-based. Substituting W for _uncached_in_flight would change an INPUT to a FITTED model without knowing what the fit was calibrated on, and it would systematically LOWER the predicted first-token time, admitting more requests, which is the direction that helps the arm under test. D187 (3) forbids exactly that: a change justified by a measured mechanism is allowed, but this one rests on an unestablished premise and happens to flatter the result. It is a finding for the user, not an overnight fix.
THE_QUEUE_INPUT_IS_THE_WRONG_QUANTITY_AN.what_would_settle_it: the fit's own regressor definition, in the D162 fitting script or its input frame. If the fit used a first-token-based queue, swapping to W is a correction; if it used completion-based, swapping is a recalibration and the coefficient must be refitted with it.

DIRECTION_NOTE: overestimating the prefix, or understating the queue, is the UNSAFE direction: it admits requests that cannot make their deadline and surfaces as LATENESS. r1 s4 has 95 on time, 2 late, 35 unsent, so there is no lateness budget to spend on a fix that errs that way.

THE_s5_RESULT_IS_MUCH_BETTER_AND_THAT_MA: s5 has only 15 recall skips against s4's 34, and against 48 for the unfixed shares arm at s5. The fix is therefore working harder at s5 than at s4. Any conclusion about the residual must be stated per seed; s6 and s7 had not landed when this was written.
